rows.title: Democrats vow to continue tax relief for CT’s working poor
rows.standfirst: Democratic leaders want permanent tax relief for CT’s working poor. The governor isn’t convinced.

rows.title: Unions: Losing public jobs will worsen CT’s race and gender pay gaps
rows.standfirst: Labor unions say state government’s shrinking workforce will exacerbate race and gender disparities, particularly involving wages.

rows.title: CT state workers to get $3,500 in bonuses under tentative deal with Lamont
rows.standfirst: The tentative deals are “strong agreements” that “will proudly be reported” to the rank-and-file for ratification, according to SEBAC.

rows.title: Deals with CT unions focus on keeping workers, not streamlining workforce
rows.standfirst: The ‘silver tsunami’ was billed as a golden opportunity to streamline state government. But now, Gov. Lamont wants to keep workers on the job.

rows.title: Gas prices in CT hit a record high; Politicians scrambling to find relief
rows.standfirst: Republicans say they will unveil a gas tax relief plan on Thursday. Democrats have met with Gov. Lamont’s administration to consider options.

rows.title: GOP lawmakers want to suspend CT’s wholesale gas tax
rows.standfirst: Republicans in the state House and Senate called Thursday for suspension of the state’s wholesale tax on gasoline, until at least July 1.

rows.title: CT added more than 55,000 jobs in 2021
rows.standfirst: Connecticut added more than 55,400 jobs in 2021, roughly 4,400 more than originally projected, the state Department of Labor reported.

rows.title: Best, or worst, of times? The battle to frame CT’s finances is underway
rows.standfirst: As elections near, the battle to frame CT’s financial situation — as the best of times or the worst of times — is expected to intensify.

rows.title: Sen. Cathy Osten: Economic aid for small towns needs a shot in the arm
rows.standfirst: The STEAP program, designed to help launch key developments in small towns, has lost its way, says one legislator who wants to revive it.

rows.title: CT lawmakers push bill to forgive unemployment ‘overpayments’
rows.standfirst: The bill would allow thousands of people to avoid repaying unemployment benefits to the state and federal government.

rows.title: CT’s government was once broke. Is it now holding too much cash?
rows.standfirst: After two years of a pandemic that battered educational and health care, businesses and households, should CT be spending more to help?

rows.title: CT companies to lawmakers: Fund child care
rows.standfirst: Electric Boat, Bigelow Tea, Hartford HealthCare are among CT employers calling for boost to social safety net spending on child care.

rows.title: Lawmakers to vote Wednesday on a gas tax holiday in Connecticut
rows.standfirst: Along with a three-month suspension of CT’s 25-cents-a-gallon tax on gasoline, a second one-week sales tax holiday on clothing is planned.

rows.title: One year’s CT budget surplus could top entire rainy day fund
rows.standfirst: State officials are feeling the pressure to share CT’s swelling budget reserves with struggling households and businesses.

rows.title: House, Senate unanimously approve CT gas tax holiday
rows.standfirst: Legislators approved a plan to provide $100 million in fuel, bus fare and sales tax relief to consumers this spring.

rows.title: Fuel tax holiday could stick CT gas stations with a big bill
rows.standfirst: Gasoline will be cheaper for CT consumers on Friday, but gas stations that fill up their own tanks this week might be selling it at a loss.

rows.title: CT contracting watchdog clears key hurdle to add investigative staff
rows.standfirst: The measure also would expand the board’s authority to probe quasi-public agencies and would shield it from emergency budget cuts.

rows.title: Good economic growth report is well-timed for Lamont and lawmakers
rows.standfirst: Lamont cited CT’s growing economy after presiding over a Bond Commission meeting in which it OK’d $666.9 million worth of borrowing.
